title: Line Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Incoming AC voltage measured by the controller is too low or too high.
fullDescription: Code E-09 is set on newer Samsung microwaves when the input voltage detection circuit measures a value outside roughly 100-130 V (North American 120 V models). The unit refuses to start because the magnetron drive expects a steady supply.

causes.cause: Sharing a circuit with a high-draw appliance
Voltage detect circuit on control board failed

symptoms: Display shows E-09 only at certain times of day
Lights dim when other appliances run

fixSteps.title: Plug into a different circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Use an extension to test the microwave on an unrelated branch circuit. If E-09 disappears, your kitchen circuit is loaded or has a wiring issue.

fixSteps.title: Measure the outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Use a plug-in voltmeter to log the voltage. Below 108 V or above 132 V indicates a supply problem.

fixSteps.title: Have an electrician check the panel
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is consistently out of range, have a licensed electrician check the neutral, breaker, and outlet. Loose neutrals are a fire hazard.

fixSteps.title: Service control board if supply is fine
fixSteps.instruction: If supply voltage is verified normal yet E-09 persists, the voltage-sense circuit on the main board is faulty; replace the board.

whenToCallPro: If you suspect a loose neutral or the outlet is warm, stop using the circuit and call a licensed electrician.

faq.a: Microwaves draw too much current for a typical UPS. Fix the supply or change circuits.
Voltage sags only occur when other big loads run on the same circuit, so the code only appears at peak times.
